description: AudioContext.baseLatency, which Blink computes as max(framesPerBuffer, renderQuantumSize) / sampleRate and caches for the life of the context (third_party/blink/renderer/modules/webaudio/audio_context.cc). Consumed by patch 0019, which replaces frames_per_buffer on the renderer's hardware parameters before anything derives from them and clears the host's hardware capability limits so they cannot clamp the claim back; the interactive latency hint passes the value through unchanged on desktop (media/base/audio_latency.cc GetInteractiveBufferSize), so the number served here is the number a page reads. Conditioned on the platform and nothing finer: the buffer is produced by the AudioManager the claimed OS runs, and the corpus shows no variation within a platform -- every Apple capture reports 256 and every Windows capture 480, across four different machines and three GPU vendors. It is NOT conditioned on media_topology, because no capture in the tree measures one machine with two different output devices, and dispersing on an unmeasured axis would be synthesis. The denominator is not ours: audio.sample_rate is undeclared, so the frame count is served over the host's own rate. See each option's note.
label: audio

options.note: MEASURED. 0.01 at 48000 Hz on the release-pin Windows 11 reference and on both NVIDIA Windows hosts, which is 480 frames exactly: WASAPI shared mode's 10 ms period. PERIOD-PINNED, unlike macOS and Linux -- 480 is 48000/100, so a real Windows machine on a 44.1 kHz device reports 441, not 480. That matters because the profile carries no sample rate (audio.sample_rate is undeclared; ledger row audio.context-sample-rate, verdict escalate), so this frame count is served over the HOST's rate: exact on a 48 kHz host, wrong on a 44.1 kHz one. Closing that row is therefore not just 'declare the rate' -- it has to decide, per platform, which of the two is pinned.

MEASURED. All five retained Apple M4 Max captures report baseLatency 0.005333333333333333 at 48000 Hz, which is 256 frames exactly, and 256 is 2 * media::limits::kMinAudioBufferSize -- what AudioManagerMac::ChooseBufferSize returns for output on macOS. FRAME-PINNED: CoreAudio holds the frame count, so the period moves with the device's rate rather than the other way round.
options.source: resources/fingerprints/raw/m4-max-chrome-20260908T163229Z.json probes['audio.properties'] = 0.005333333333333333 at 48000 Hz; media/audio/mac/audio_manager_mac.cc ChooseBufferSize with media/base/limits.h

options.note: AUTHORED, NOT MEASURED: Chromium's own Linux floor, not a capture. kMinimumOutputBufferSize is 512 in media/audio/pulse/audio_manager_pulse.cc, and AudioManagerPulse::GetPreferredOutputStreamParameters starts there and only ever raises it; media/base/audio_latency.cc states the same thing in prose -- 'On Linux, the minimum hardware buffer size is 512'. WHY NO MEASUREMENT EXISTS: all four admitted NVIDIA Linux references enumerate ZERO audio devices, against an audiooutput on every macOS and Windows reference, so their 44100 Hz / 441 frames is the no-sound-card path and not a Linux desktop -- the renderer's invalid-parameter reset is 48000/480 and 480 scaled by 44100/48000 is exactly 441. The only Linux capture in the tree holding a real audio device is the non-admissible v1 linux-ws at 48000/2048, which is ALSA's compiled default (kDefaultOutputBufferSize in media/audio/alsa/audio_manager_alsa.cc) and is also this project's own build host, so inheriting it would preserve exactly the host tell this axis exists to remove. WHAT WOULD REPLACE THIS: one headed capture from a Linux desktop that has a real audio output device, admitted through capture/. On PulseAudio or pipewire-pulse the expected reading is 512 frames at the server's rate; measure it and this option becomes physical-ground-truth or is corrected.
